title: Psychotherapy providers in Germany
intro: Several professions offer psychotherapy in Germany, and knowing the differences helps you find suitable help. Statutory health insurance pays for treatment by licensed providers using approved methods. Waiting times can be long, but there are ways to shorten the search. This article gives a general overview; rules change, so check current details.

sections.heading: Who provides psychotherapy
paragraphs: Psychological psychotherapists have a university degree in psychology and further training in psychotherapy. Medical psychotherapists are doctors with additional training, including specialists in psychosomatic medicine and psychiatry, who may also prescribe medicines. Child and adolescent psychotherapists treat young people. Only licensed professionals can bill insurance.

sections.heading: Approved methods
paragraphs: Health insurance covers behavioural therapy, depth psychology-based therapy, analytic psychotherapy and, since 2020, systemic therapy. Each approach works differently, for example behavioural therapy focuses on current patterns and skills, whereas psychodynamic therapy explores underlying conflicts. The choice depends on your problem and preference, and the therapist can explain.

sections.heading: How to start
paragraphs: You can contact practices directly or begin with a consultation hour, in which a therapist assesses your needs and recommends the next step. After a few trial sessions, the therapy is applied for with your insurer. Short-term therapy, long-term therapy and group therapy are available, depending on the case. The appointment service reachable under 116117 can help find an initial appointment.

sections.heading: Shortening the wait
paragraphs: Contact several therapists, ask to be placed on waiting lists and ask about cancellations. Your insurer can help with searching. Counselling centres, outpatient clinics and day clinics may offer faster support. Private therapists and online programmes are alternatives, but check qualifications and costs.

sections.heading: Practical points
paragraphs: Therapy is confidential. Interpreters are not always covered, so ask about language support and specialised services for refugees. Do not stop medication on your own, and say if you do not feel a good fit with the therapist, since the relationship matters for success.

examples.title: Making the first call
examples.text: Imagine you decide to look for a therapist. You could call five practices during their telephone hours, describe your main concern briefly and ask for a consultation hour.

examples.title: Choosing a method
examples.text: Suppose two therapists offer different approaches. You might ask each how they would work on your problem and how long therapy would likely take.
